articles.title: UCLA cheerleaders steal the spotlight from undefeated football team in viral video
articles.summary: UCLA's football team is undefeated, but it's their cheerleaders who are stealing the spotlight! A slow-motion video of three UCLA dancers during the Bruins' victory over Illinois has exploded online, racking up more than 28 million views!
articles.body:
UCLA's football team is undefeated, but it's their cheerleaders who are stealing the spotlight! A slow-motion video of three UCLA dancers during the Bruins' victory over Illinois has exploded online, racking up more than 28 million views!

The clip was shared by an Ohio State fan account with a hilarious caption: "Transferring to UCLA!"

The dancers are Quillan Casem, Hayleigh Liu, and Sharlize True Trujillo, who was crowned Miss California 2026! UCLA may be undefeated, but these three are winning the internet!

articles.title: Is Andrej Stojakovic related to former NBA player Peja? Everything to know about Illinois star
articles.standfirst: Stojakovic scored a record-setting 46 points against Duke in their home arena.
articles.summary: Stojakovic scored a record-setting 46 points against Duke in their home arena.
articles.body:
Tuesday night featured a - literally - historic performance at Cameron Indoor Stadium in Durham, North Carolina. The No. 5 North Carolina Tar Heels welcomed the No. 10 Illinois Fighting Illini and got crushed 99--78 . Losing by that much at home is one thing, but the way in which it happened was the true storyline.

Andrej Stojakovic , who alternated between a starting and bench role last season for Illinois, put together a 46-point performance in the team's win over Duke on Tuesday night. Quentin Coleman scored 27 points, and no other Illinois player reached double-digits. Stojakovic's 46 points were the most ever scored by an opponent on the road at Duke .

Andrej Stojakovic sets record for most points scored by an opponent at Duke

Stojakovic's previous career-high was 37 points , which he put up against Stanford during the second round of the 2025 ACC Tournament , when he was a member of the California Golden Bears . Stojakovic has taken a big step forward in his development here in his senior season, now that more of the offensive load is on his plate.

For those NBA fans who remember his last name, Andrej is in fact Peja Stojakovic's son . Peja was one of the best shooters in NBA history, and made three straights All-Star teams as a member of the Sacramento Kings . He won the 2011 NBA Championship with the Dallas Mavericks , in his final season in the league.

Andrej is a different player than his father, relying more on his slashing ability and adeptness finishing at the rim . But this season so far, he's shooting 37.5% from three-point range , which is a big step up from his past three seasons. The sky appears to be the limit for Andrej as he gets ready for the NBA jump next year.

articles.title: Deion Sanders’ daughter opens up emotionally about living with a lifelong condition: “I wish I was just normal”
articles.standfirst: The Hall of Famer's youngest daughter has had diabetes since she was thirteen
articles.summary: The Hall of Famer's youngest daughter has had diabetes since she was thirteen
articles.body:
The 2026 NCAA football season for the Colorado Buffaloes has unfolded with far less national fanfare than the chaotic, celebrity-filled circus that defined the program’s earlier years. Sitting at a 4-6 record (2-5 in Big 12 play) with just two regular-season games remaining against Cincinnati and UCF, head coach Deion Sanders has already surpassed last year’s dismal 3-9 finish.

Yet, despite selling out their season ticket allotment in Boulder before the campaign even kicked off, the Buffaloes have largely faded into national irrelevance as the early-era hype continues to cool down. Away from the gridiron spotlight in Boulder, however, Sanders’ youngest daughter, Shelomi Sanders , just captured widespread attention with a deeply personal and emotional revelation about her own daily battles.

Shelomi Sanders Opens Up About Living With Type 1 Diabetes

A collegiate basketball guard who previously competed at the Division I level with Jackson State, Colorado, and Alabama A&M before transferring to Colorado State University Pueblo , Shelomi Sanders has spent her entire life under the glare of sports cameras.

This week the 22-year-old athlete shared a raw, heartfelt reflection on Instagram detailing her nearly decade-long struggle with Type 1 diabetes , an autoimmune condition she was first diagnosed with at age 13. “Diabetes, you came into my life when I was just 13 and nothing has been the same since, ” she wrote in the candid caption.

You’ve brought tears, frustration, and countless battles nobody sees. Some days I wish I was just normal, but what really is normal? Now I see things differently.

Her path to understanding the chronic illness began with a terrifying medical scare nine years ago. At 13, Shelomi started dropping weight rapidly, drinking nearly two gallons of water a day , and battling severe fatigue, symptoms she initially mistook for the byproduct of intense offseason workouts alongside her Hall of Fame father.

When she suddenly began vomiting and couldn’t even hold down basic cold medicine, she was rushed to the emergency room, where doctors discovered her blood sugar levels had spiked past a dangerous 600 mg/dL.

Today, balancing college athletics with round-the- clock glucose monitoring and insulin management , even while asleep, Shelomi uses her platform and an NIL partnership with Dexcom U to dismantle misconceptions about diabetes and prove to young athletes that a lifelong diagnosis does not have to limit their dreams.

articles.title: LeBron’s son Bryce James falls out of the Arizona rotation following the coach’s decision
articles.standfirst: Bryce played in three of the first four games and scored a total of only eight points.
articles.summary: Bryce played in three of the first four games and scored a total of only eight points.
articles.body:
Navigating the early stages of a collegiate basketball career at a perennial powerhouse like the Arizona Wildcats is never an easy task, and sophomore guard Bryce James is learning that reality firsthand.

Despite scouts long projecting his physical frame and long-term upside as having a higher ceiling than his older brother Bronny , who currently occupies a deep-bench role in the NBA with minimal court time, Bryce has struggled to carve out consistent minutes or signature moments in Tucson.

After redshirting without logging a single regular-season appearance as a freshman, James started Arizona’s first three contests this fall before not playing due to coach’s decision during Friday’s gritty 80-69 victory over the Auburn Tigers .

With the No. 12 Wildcats sitting at a 3-1 record , having bounced back with three consecutive wins following a season-opening loss to UCLA . head coach Tommy Lloyd now prepares his roster for its toughest test yet tonight against the powerhouse No. 3 UConn Huskies .

Bryce James Reacts to Major Arizona Recruiting News

Even while fighting to earn back his spot in Lloyd’s rotation, James remains heavily invested in the long-term trajectory of the program. Through three games played during the 2026–27 campaign, the Akron, Ohio native has averaged 2.7 points, 1.7 assists, and 1.3 steals across 12.0 minutes per contest.

Ahead of tonight’s marquee clash against UConn at the McKale Center , the Wildcats secured a massive recruiting victory when five-star Class of 2027 prospect Adan Diggs officially committed to Arizona over finalists Arkansas, Kentucky, and USC.

Ranked as the No. 1 shooting guard and a top-five overall player nationally in the 2027 cycle, the 6-foot-4 standout out of Goodyear, Arizona represents a huge backcourt addition for the future.

Bryce James wasted zero time celebrating the news, resharing the commitment graphic on his Instagram story accompanied by an enthusiastic “Yuhhhhhhh” reaction.

While adding another elite perimeter weapon means future competition for backcourt touches will only intensify next season , James is clearly embracing the team-first culture in Tucson as he works to prove he belongs on the floor for Arizona basketball right now.

articles.title: Michigan WR Andrew Marsh faces indecent exposure charge: Will he play again this season?
articles.standfirst: Marsh is listed as questionable for Saturday’s game against UCLA; Michigan has not announced a suspension
articles.summary: Marsh is listed as questionable for Saturday’s game against UCLA; Michigan has not announced a suspension
articles.body:
Michigan wide receiver Andrew Marsh is facing a misdemeanor indecent exposure charge stemming from a February incident.

Case remains pending, with an arraignment and pretrial proceedings scheduled for Dec. 2 in 14A District Court. The charge is an allegation, not a finding of guilt.

Pittsfield Township police said a food delivery driver reported the incident on Feb. 2. According to the department, she told officers that a man answered the door with a blanket around his shoulders and was unclothed underneath.

As she turned to leave, the man allegedly pulled the blanket open . Police said the customer later sent her a message calling her attractive and asking her to return. Officers identified the resident as the suspect, according to the police account.

The Washtenaw County Prosecutor’s Office authorized a misdemeanor complaint on Oct. 14. Court records cited in reports list arraignment and pretrial proceedings for Dec. 2. The University of Michigan said it had just learned of the incident and would monitor the case, but could not comment further while it is ongoing.

Will he play against UCLA?

The sophomore was listed as questionable on Michigan’s initial availability report for Saturday’s game. That designation does not establish whether the pending case affects his playing status, and the university has not announced a suspension.

JJ Buchanan, Michigan’s leading receiver in yardage, is out with a shoulder injury, making the question of who will be available at receiver especially relevant.

The Texas native leads Michigan with 48 catches through 10 games, totaling 459 yards and one touchdown. As a freshman in 2025, he recorded 45 receptions for 651 yards and four touchdowns.

If he is unavailable against UCLA , the Wolverines would be without one of their most productive pass-catchers as they head into the final stretch of the regular season.

Under Michigan law, the misdemeanor charge carries a maximum penalty of one year in jail, a fine of up to $1,000, or both . That is the statutory maximum, not a prediction of what a court would impose.

The complaint reported so far is for misdemeanor indecent exposure; no conviction has been reported.

Any team or university discipline would be a separate decision from the court case. Michigan has said it is monitoring the situation, but has not disclosed what action, if any, it may take.

No suspension has been announced, and the case’s outcome and the school’s response will shape what happens to the receiver’s season.
